**3.4  Edge Case** 

**3.4.1  Edge Case Handling – Sensor Failure Detection and Crash Prevention**

**![][image1]**Detects missing or invalid sensor data.

* Immediately set the robot speed to 0\.  
* Maintain a stationary state until sensor data is restored.  
* Automatically resume the previous operating state.

**Metrics Used to Validate Performance**

**Notes：**Detection and Stop Command Response Times are based on the confirmed 10 ms EV3 monitoring interval.

| Trial | Detection Time (ms) | Stop Command (ms) | Physical Stop (ms) | Crash Prevention |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | 10 | 10 | 86 | **Success** |
| 2 | 10 | 10 | 92 | **Success** |
| 3 | 10 | 10 | 78 | **Success** |
| 4 | 10 | 10 | 105 | **Success** |
| 5 | 10 | 10 | 89 | **Success** |
| **Avarage** | 10 | 10 | 90 | **Success** |
| **Success Rate** | \- | \- | \- | **100%** |

* The testing results demonstrate that the robot consistently detects sensor failure and initiates the stopping procedure within the 10 ms monitoring interval.  
* The average physical stopping time was 90 ms across five trials.   
* The robot also successfully resumed its previous operating state in all five trials, achieving a 100% automatic recovery success rate.

**3.4.2 Edge Case Handling – Abnormal Motion Crash Detection and Recovery**

**Edge Case Situations** 

| Testing Scenario  | Abnormal Condition  | Expected Behaviour  |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| **Stuck at Inner Wall Corner**  | The robot becomes trapped at the inner wall corner.  | Detect abnormal motion and activate recovery.  |
| **Stuck at Outer Wall Corner**  | The robot encounters resistance at the outer wall corner.  | Detect abnormal motion and activate recovery.  |
| **Stuck at Inner Wall Vertex**  | Restricted turning space prevents the robot from changing direction.  | Detect the blockage and attempt recovery.  |
| **Manual Pressure Applied**  | External pressure prevents the robot from moving normally.  | Detect the lack of movement and increase motor power.  |

**Edge Case Solution**

![][image2]

**Encoder-Based Monitoring:** Monitors wheel movement using Motor Encoder Feedback.

* **Time-Based Detection:** Uses a timer to detect prolonged periods without movement.  
* **Enhanced Motor Response:** Applies speed × \-5 to generate stronger forward driving force.  
* **Automatic Recovery:** Automatically activates recovery during Wall Tracking to overcome resistance.

**Metrics Used to Validate Performance**

**Notes:** The 300 ms Stuck Detection Time is based on the predefined timer threshold configured in the robot's program

| Trial  | Testing Scenario | Pressure Duration (s) | Detection Threshold (ms) | Recovery Time (s) | Result |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | Stuck at Inner Wall corner | \- | 300 ms | 10 | **Success** |
| 2 | Stuck at Outer Wall corner | \- | 300 ms | 5 | **Success** |
| 3 | Stuck at Inner Wall vertex | \- | 300 ms | \- | **Failed** |
| 4 | Manual pressure applied | Released immediately after power increase | 300 ms | 2 | **Success** |
| 5 | Manual pressure applied | 5s after power increase | 300 ms | 2 | **Success** |
| 6 | Manual pressure applied | 10s after power increase | 300 ms | 2 | **Success** |
| **Average** | 5 successful trials | \- | 300 ms | 4.2 | \- |
| **Success Rate** | 5/6 trials | \- | \- | \- | **83.3%** |

**Engineering Decisions:**

* The testing results demonstrate that the robot detects abnormal motion and automatically increases motor power after reaching the detection threshold.  
* The average recovery time was 4.2 seconds across five successful trials.  
* The robot **successfully recovered in five out of six trials**, achieving an **83.3% recovery success** rate.

One trial failed because the robot became trapped at the Inner Wall vertex, where the restricted angle prevented it from changing direction.
